travelAdvisory.summary:
Reissued after periodic review with minor edits.
Exercise normal precautions in Australia.
Read the country information page for additional information on travel to Australia.
If you decide to travel to Australia:

Enroll in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP) to receive alerts and make it easier to locate you in an emergency.
Review the Country Security Report for Australia.
Prepare a plan for emergency situations. Review the Traveler’s Checklist.

healthcare.costForTourists: Excellent quality. US citizens pay full price (no Medicare reciprocity). GP visit $50-100 AUD. ER: treated regardless but billed — $300-1,000+ AUD. Reciprocal Healthcare Agreements with UK, NZ, and some EU countries.
healthcare.pharmacyAccess: Pharmacies (chemists) like Priceline and Chemist Warehouse everywhere. Good range of OTC medications. Pharmacists are well-trained.
healthcare.hospitalNotes: World-class hospitals in all major cities. Flying Doctor Service covers remote outback areas. Healthcare in remote/outback areas is limited — evacuation may be needed.
healthcare.insuranceAdvice: Travel insurance essential for US citizens — no reciprocal healthcare agreement. Medical bills can be very expensive without insurance.

controlledSubstances.note: Prescription-only since 2018 (was previously OTC). Cannot be purchased at pharmacies without Australian prescription.
Available only at pharmacies with ID (tracked due to methamphetamine concerns).
Medical cannabis legal with prescription. Recreational use varies by state — decriminalized in ACT, illegal elsewhere. Don't bring CBD products.

medications.generalAdvice: Australia has strict biosecurity laws — declare ALL medications at customs. Bring prescriptions and a doctor's letter. Border Force takes undeclared medications seriously.

scams.name: Drop bear joke
scams.description: Not a scam — Australians will tell you about 'drop bears' (fictional aggressive koalas). This is just Australian humor.
scams.avoidance: Laugh along. It's a rite of passage.

scams.name: Rental car excess insurance upsell
scams.description: Rental car companies push expensive excess reduction insurance ($30-50/day) at the counter. Makes a $50/day rental cost $100.
scams.avoidance: Buy standalone excess reduction insurance online before your trip ($5-8/day from providers like RentalCover) or use your credit card's coverage.

scams.name: Opal/Myki card confusion
scams.description: Tourists buy single-journey tickets at a huge premium instead of getting a reusable transport card that's much cheaper per trip.
scams.avoidance: Get an Opal card (Sydney) or Myki card (Melbourne) immediately at the airport or any station.

connectivity.simOptions: Telstra (best coverage), Optus, or Vodafone SIM at airports. $20-40 AUD for 30 days. eSIM via Airalo. Telstra has the only decent outback coverage.
connectivity.wifiAvailability: Free WiFi at most cafes, restaurants, and libraries. Australian data plans are more expensive than Asia/Europe.
connectivity.bestOption: Telstra SIM if going outside cities. Optus or eSIM for cities only.

cultural.tipping: Not expected or common. Australians are paid living wages. Rounding up at restaurants is appreciated but never expected. No tip jars.
cultural.dressCode: Very casual. Thongs (flip-flops) and shorts are acceptable almost everywhere. Smart casual for upscale restaurants. Sun protection is essential.
cultural.greetings: 'G'day' or 'Hey, how ya going?' Handshake. Very informal culture. First names immediately, even in business.
taboos: Not wearing sunscreen (skin cancer rates are highest in the world)
Being pretentious or boastful ('tall poppy syndrome')
cultural.haggling: Not practiced. Prices are fixed. Only at weekend markets and garage sales.

safety.lgbtSafety: Same-sex marriage legal since 2017. Very tolerant. Sydney has one of the world's largest Mardi Gras celebrations.
safety.soloFemaleSafety: Very safe. Australia is one of the safest countries for solo travelers.
safety.notes: Australia is very safe. The main dangers are natural — extreme heat, bushfires, dangerous wildlife (snakes, spiders, box jellyfish, crocodiles in the north), and rip currents at beaches. Always swim between the flags at patrolled beaches.

practical.visaFreeCountries: US citizens: ETA required ($20 AUD), 90 days. UK: eVisitor, free, 90 days. NZ: unlimited.
practical.bestTimeToVisit: September-November (spring) and March-May (autumn). Summer (Dec-Feb) is hot. Seasons are reversed from Northern Hemisphere.
